transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I’m here because of elevators, honestly. I know that probably sounds kind of silly, especially because I do know, in my head, that elevators aren’t really dangerous most of the time. Like, I can tell myself that people ride them every day and nothing happens.

But when I actually have to get in one, it’s like my body doesn’t listen to that. I get really scared that I’m going to be trapped in there, like the doors are going to close and I won’t be able to get out. And I just can’t make myself feel normal about it, no matter how much I try to talk myself down. It’s been bothering me enough that I figured I should come talk to someone about it.
Is your fear mostly limited to elevators, or do you also experience similar anxiety in other situations, like in crowded places, social settings, or when you’re away from home?

It’s really mostly elevators. Like, I don’t feel that same kind of fear just being out somewhere or around people or anything like that. It’s specifically when I’m faced with getting into an elevator, because even though I know they’re not actually dangerous most of the time, my mind goes straight to, what if I get stuck, what if the doors close and I can’t get out.

And I know that probably doesn’t make a lot of sense when I say it out loud, because I can understand logically that people use them every day. But in that moment, it just feels like I’m going to be trapped, and I can’t make myself calm down or feel normal about it. So yeah, it’s really centered on elevators.
